records.title: 交班餐厅
records.status: first-pass concept reviewed; remaining spatial issues recorded in review.md
records.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a NEW concept-art development sheet for GUIHANG, an original enormous interstellar mothership that is a living civilian community. Reinterpret the supplied small common-room image into a populated NEIGHBORHOOD SHIFT MESS. The second image is the mothership exterior; use it solely for its original industrial form language. These are visual references, not layouts to copy. Preserve warm ivory removable panels, blue-gray paired structural ribs, graphite recesses, a few faded brick-red identifier blocks, restrained amber service details. The old eight-seat room and its empty-ship scale MUST NOT carry over.

Art direction: beautiful professional hand-drawn science-fiction environment concept painting, confident graphite and fine ink construction lines, selectively opaque gouache and marker color, warm off-white sketchbook background, crisp designed forms with calm large surfaces and localized machinery. Cinematic sophistication, human warmth, believable original industrial spacecraft identity. Not a game screenshot, not photorealism, not a luxurious mall, not medieval or steampunk. Show repair history but not filth.

Sheet: landscape approximately 3:2. A single generous immersive main perspective occupies about 80 percent; a narrow bottom strip has two clearly separate detail vignettes, one replaceable table/seating assembly and one serving/return threshold. These are concept details, not a false precise floor-plan. Only title "GUIHANG / SHIFT MESS" and tiny vignette titles "TABLE MODULE" and "SERVICE EDGE"; no other text, no numeric dimensions, no invented engineering diagram.

Scene: eye level around 1.6 m with a calm wide 28 mm perspective from a broad clear foreground passage into a long, inhabited mess. The local ceiling is comfortable and lofty, roughly two ordinary room heights, not cathedral scale. Three repeated blue-gray portal ribs give rhythm and recognizable spacecraft framing. About ten modest four-to-six-seat table islands with readable human-sized seats in the room, most partly occupied; twenty to thirty diverse adult residents in small varied groups. People have convincing natural anatomy and distinct silhouettes; prioritize readable group behavior over tiny portrait detail. A tired maintenance worker has put down a jacket and is handed a hot bowl. Two off-duty residents talk by an alcove; a cultivation worker wheels a CLOSED produce trolley on the service edge. Clothing combines practical gray/blue workwear with varied casual muted garments, not identical uniforms. People sitting, standing and walking coexist without clogging the circulation.

Left side: recessed galley and serving counter, a clearly separate tray-return niche near the entry; queue stays beside the counter. Right: quieter booth niches under insulated wall panels and a small pinned community collage with no readable writing. Far end: an ordinary large personnel bulkhead doorway continues to the residential passage, entirely within the same pressure/gravity compartment; visibly human-scaled. Central and side passages stay open. Several tables, rather than one ceremonial banquet table. Warm task lights over people, cooler maintenance recesses, a small area of living plants protected from traffic. Wooden-tone repairable composite tabletops and textile acoustic panels are subordinate accents, not wood architecture. Every bench, shelf and light has a credible attachment.

Gravity: this is a local room in a candidate rotating habitat module; people share one local floor direction, feet on floor. Do not draw the global ring, fixed-axis connection, weightless props, starfield windows, glass roof, an exterior planet, or any implied magical gravity mechanism. Hundreds of residents are a setting hypothesis across the ship, not all crammed into this room. Convey a real neighborhood that has places beyond the frame, with an inviting lived-in scale and controlled visual hierarchy.

records.title: 居住街廊
records.status: first-pass concept reviewed; remaining spatial issues recorded in review.md
records.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Develop a new GUIHANG mothership interior concept sheet: HABITATION LANE, using the supplied previous small common-room and exterior sheets ONLY as industrial design and hand-painted presentation references. Completely change the composition and subject; do not repeat the old eight-person dining room. This is an original inhabited interstellar civilization-home. The current design hypothesis is several hundred awake residents across many neighborhoods, with seven focal story characters, not seven people in an empty giant ship.

Style: professional science-fiction production concept artwork, confident graphite/ink construction drawing with selective opaque gouache and subdued marker washes on warm off-white paper; compelling architectural perspective and warm lived-in atmosphere. Keep the same ivory removable panels, blue-gray structural portal ribs, graphite service recesses, sparse brick-red panel IDs, amber grip/service details; broad calm surfaces with localized mechanical density. Original industrial spacefaring elegance, not a shopping mall, prison corridor, hotel, submarine, fantasy castle or cyberpunk neon.

Layout: landscape approximately 3:2. One big immersive perspective uses upper 80% of sheet; bottom 20% contains two small detached detail studies of a PERSONAL DOOR ALCOVE and an integrated REPAIR BENCH. Only title "GUIHANG / HABITATION LANE" plus "DOOR ALCOVE" and "REPAIR BENCH". No other writing, no numbered dimensions, no deceptive engineering floor plan.

Main view: camera standing at 1.6 m looking diagonally along a gently following residential passage inside one local habitat segment, comfortable broad pedestrian aisle around three persons across. A limited two-deck neighborhood: inhabited cabins open onto the main passage, with ONE clearly guarded upper balcony/gallery and one believable straight staircase at the far end, stair rail continuous, no labyrinth. Ceiling modestly high over the central passage; upper cabin ceiling heights believable, no vaulted megacathedral. Strong repeated ribs and careful perspective rhythm lead to a small shared reading/work niche in the background. Upper walkway has full-height safe guardrails with mesh/infill, no unprotected edge. Foot traffic remains unobstructed.

Show around 12 to 18 ordinary residents in convincing varied actions, natural proportions and restrained faces. Foreground left, someone sits on a fold-down bench repairing a coat; a companion stands beside them, with fabric/tool tray entirely inside the niche. Midground a resident carries clean folded linen back to their door; two people converse near a recessed community notice board, which only contains abstract pinned cards. Another person has returned from a shift carrying a closed lunch container. One older resident reads quietly in a recessed seat. A few people on the upper gallery make the social scale legible. Practical muted civilian clothes mixed with a few work overalls; people are not soldiers in parade formation. Focus on everyday relationships without inventing a lore event.

Private life: thick human-scaled cabin doors spaced sensibly, quiet acoustic fabric just inside a partly open doorway, removable personal nameplate slots with NO legible writing, coats/shoes in recessed lockers, a couple of small hand-kept plants under task lamps, patched fabric and differing personal keepsakes. No bedrooms fully exposed to the main circulation. One access panel is being serviced behind a portable low barrier in a side bay, not blocking the exit. Distant fire/pressure bulkhead is within this same habitat reference frame. Do not turn all doors into massive hangar gates.

Gravity and setting: everyone stands on the same local floor, a room segment within a candidate rotating habitat; global ship gravity is not resolved. Show no global rotating ring, no impossible ordinary doorway into a fixed spindle, no floating cups. No starfield window, panoramic space glass, fake daylight sky, giant indoor tree or urban boulevard. Lighting is shipboard warm wall/task light against restrained cool structural shade. Convey the particular pleasure of returning to your own familiar corner of an enormous spacecraft.

records.title: 培养区与公共生活
records.status: first-pass concept reviewed; remaining spatial issues recorded in review.md
records.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a new original GUIHANG mothership environment concept-art sheet, CULTIVATION COMMONS. Use the two supplied old GUIHANG sheets as visual language and traditional hand-drawn presentation references only; transform the subject and layout completely. Design a humane connection between a small public neighborhood commons and a protected operational cultivation compartment aboard a huge spacefaring civilization-home. Several hundred awake residents across the ship are a working hypothesis, not a capacity verified by this picture.

Art medium: sophisticated production concept art in fine ink, graphite construction lines, opaque gouache/marker color on warm off-white paper. Beautiful composed architecture, tactile repairable details, emotionally inviting but unmistakably spacecraft. Palette follows GUIHANG: warm ivory modular panels, blue-gray load ribs, graphite service recesses, few brick-red wayfinding panels, amber work details. Vegetation adds fresh restrained greens; soft warm public-area lights contrast with crisp neutral-white grow lights. No pink neon grow-room spectacle, no fantasy jungle, no luxury glass atrium, no photorealistic render.

Sheet layout: wide landscape roughly 3:2, main eye-level perspective takes about 80%; slim bottom strip has two clearly separate construction vignettes: "CLEAN TRANSFER" and "GROW RACK". Title only "GUIHANG / CULTIVATION COMMONS", no long text, no figures claiming crop yield, no numerical scale or misleading exact engineering diagram.

Main perspective: camera in the public commons, around 1.6 m, looking along a continuous thick pressure-compatible internal glazed wall. On LEFT beyond the continuous glass is a visibly separate controlled cultivation room: parallel waist-high hydroponic leaf-crop beds in modular racks, adequate full standing aisles, retractable neutral grow lamps, visible fluid/air service manifold in a protected side spine. Rows extend to a plausible closed back wall, not infinite. Two or three technicians in clean light gray working garments and hair coverings are maintaining trays INSIDE; everyone there is in clean work mode.

On RIGHT of the continuous glazing, the public strip has broad clear circulation and a couple of modest sitting/table alcoves anchored to the floor. Around 10 to 15 residents total across foreground/background, a few quietly talking or sketching plant shapes, one off-duty worker eating at a two-person table OUTSIDE the glazing. Natural diverse adult human proportions. There is no cafeteria table inside production. A person pauses to see a technician tending a tray through the glass: a warm but subtle interaction across the real boundary. A freestanding public herb pot is clearly a small decorative/learning specimen on the PUBLIC side, never presented as part of controlled production.

Critical readable threshold: toward the mid-background at the END of the glazed wall, show a clearly enclosed personnel hygiene vestibule with TWO offset closed doors and a small visible hand-cleaning/dedicated-workwear niche, connecting public circulation and the cultivation room; no open doorway punching directly through the glazed wall. In the nearer partition incorporate a SMALL sealed pass-through material hatch with framed observation glass at trolley height, with a closed hard-sided produce trolley waiting on the public side. The small hatch is not a person-sized shortcut. Keep visitor path, grow-room worker aisle, and material transfer legible as three distinct uses. No loose hoses trailing into public traffic.

Structure: substantial repeated blue-gray ribs and accessible utility panels, local ceiling modest, insulated solid outer structure behind the growing equipment. Internal glass is for observing a neighboring room, NOT a window into outer space. All areas are within the SAME candidate rotating habitat segment and local floor direction; do not depict global gravity machinery, magic floors or a rotation-to-fixed connection. This is ONE useful cultivation compartment and its community edge, not proof of a complete closed ecology or whole-ship food sufficiency. Convey technical care and ordinary residents finding pleasure in green living things.

records.edit_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
The single supplied image is the EDIT TARGET: GUIHANG / CULTIVATION COMMONS concept sheet. Make ONE focused architectural correction in TWO matching regions. Preserve the large scene's viewpoint, ALL foreground people, tables, plants, continuous glass partition, grow racks, trolley, small pass-through hatch, materials, palette, lettering at top, ink/gouache rendering, bottom-right GROW RACK study and overall page composition. Do not redraw the whole scene or add new subjects.

Problem: the main scene's distant open CULTIVATION ACCESS doorway currently suggests an unclear straight-through route, while the bottom-left CLEAN TRANSFER image suggests another unrelated room with confusing doors. Replace these two depictions with the SAME simple two-door hygiene vestibule.

1) In the main scene ONLY change the distant doorway area underneath/just left of the CULTIVATION ACCESS marking, beyond the public tables and at the far end of the glass partition. Fill the currently wide OPEN front aperture with one CLOSED, human-sized ivory/blue-gray personnel door seated inside the existing thick frame, with a small narrow vertical observation window and visible continuous frame. Retain the existing external wall and sign. This is the PUBLIC entrance door to the hygiene vestibule. Do not show any straight-through open back door. The cultivation exit is around the LEFT side inside the vestibule, so it is not directly visible from the public commons. Public circulation outside remains open. No extra door beside this entrance.

2) Replace ONLY the entire bottom-left CLEAN TRANSFER vignette with a clear small ISOMETRIC CUTAWAY concept of that same vestibule, on the same ivory sketchbook paper. Match main-scene ivory panels, blue-gray door frames and brick-red accent. A compact rectangular enclosed chamber with its roof and a limited part of right wall cut away for viewing. It has EXACTLY TWO doors:
- the public door on the FRONT wall, matching the door just added to the main scene: CLOSED, vertical narrow window; indicate the public approach outside it with a short arrow and small label PUBLIC.
- the cultivation door on the LEFT wall, placed toward the BACK half of that wall so the route turns left; CLOSED with the same human-scale frame; outside this left wall show just one partial green grow-rack edge, with a short arrow and small label GROW.
The solid BACK wall contains a wash basin with tap and splash panel, NOT a third door. The right wall carries a small closed clean-workwear cabinet and short change bench. One simple unobtrusive standing human silhouette establishes scale. Room contents do not block the L-shaped route from front door to left door. Both door leaves closed. No open bypass, third door, central portal, or long tunnel. Show only this limited architectural relationship, no detailed engineering dimensions, no pressure or sterility certification.
Keep the existing vignette title CLEAN TRANSFER below. Only additional text PUBLIC and GROW. Match the existing professional hand-drawn construction and muted colors. The bottom-right GROW RACK drawing and all other sheet contents remain unchanged.
